Rossie D. Alston Jr.

KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

Defendants.

PLAINTIFE’S MOTION FOR LEAVE TO FILE SUR-REPLY
TO DEFENDANT META PLATFORMS, INC.’S REPLY
IN SUPPORT OF MOTION TO DISMISS

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves the Court, under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1), for leave
to file the Proposed Sur-Reply attached as Exhibit A. The Proposed Sur-Reply answers one
argument that Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”) raised for the first time in its Reply
Memorandum filed August 31, 2026 (ECF No. 39). In support, Plaintiff states as follows.

1. Meta moved to dismiss the First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5) on August 21,
2026 (ECF Nos. 21, 22). Plaintiff filed his opposition on August 24, 2026 (ECF No. 30). Meta
filed its Reply on August 31, 2026 (ECF No. 39).

2. Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) provides for an opening memorandum, an opposition,
and a reply. After that, “[nJo further briefs or written communications may be filed without first

obtaining leave of Court.”

9/1/2026

3. Meta’s Reply largely reiterates or develops arguments advanced in its opening
memorandum, or responds to arguments in Plaintiff’s opposition. Plaintiff seeks no additional
round of briefing on those matters.

4. One argument is different. At page 7, Meta argues for the first time that Count IV
fails because Plaintiff “has not identified any non-speculative opportunity for him to provide
testimony in any action,” and that “[t]he FAC’s failure to identify any actual testimony in federal
court that Plaintiff has or likely will offer independently dooms Plaintiff’s Section 1985(2) claim.”
ECF No. 39 at 7. Meta rests that argument on later procedural developments: the dismissal of the
286 Action and the pending motion to dismiss in the 376 Action. Id.

3. Meta’s opening memorandum did not advance that argument. It argued that
Plaintiff had not pleaded injury because he continued to litigate. ECF No. 22 at 12. It suggested in
a footnote that “attending court” might require physical presence at a proceeding. Id. at 12 n.1. It
did not argue that a prospective witness must plead a presently identifiable and sufficiently certain
future occasion to testify. It did not argue that the FAC fails for want of allegations identifying
testimony Plaintiff “has or likely will offer.” And it did not treat later procedural events in the
underlying actions as a test of Plaintiff’s witness status. Plaintiff therefore has had no opportunity
to respond.

6. The Proposed Sur-Reply is confined to that one argument. It introduces no new
evidence. It relies only on the existing Rule 12 record, principally the First Amended Complaint
and Meta’s Reply.

7. Plaintiff does not request a hearing on this Motion and waives oral argument. The
Motion is procedural and confined to a single question, and the written submissions present it in

full. Plaintiff therefore submits the Motion for decision on the papers pursuant to Federal Rule of

Civil Procedure 78(b) and Local Civil Rule 7(J). Because no hearing is sought, Plaintiff does not
seek a hearing date under Local Civil Rule 7(E).

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court grant leave pursuant to Local
Civil Rule 7(F)(1) to file the Proposed Sur-Reply attached as Exhibit A and deem the Proposed

Sur-Reply filed as of the date of the Court’s Order. A memorandum in support and a proposed

order accompany this Motion.

Date: September 1, 2026 Respectfully submitted,
